rows.note: Use this as the everyday all-purpose term for a prescription slip or medicine order, but not for an eyeglass-lens prescription.

example.english: The doctor gave me a prescription and told me to pick up the medicine downstairs.
example.traditional: 醫生開咗藥單，叫我去樓下攞藥。
example.jyutping: ji1 saang1 hoi1 zo2 joek6 daan1 giu3 ngo5 heoi3 lau4 haa6 lo2 joek6

rows.note: Use this instead of 藥單 in formal or clinical language for the written medical order, including an eyeglass prescription.

example.english: The optometrist has made the glasses according to the prescription.
example.traditional: 驗眼師已經按照處方配好副眼鏡。
example.jyutping: jim6 ngaan5 si1 ji5 ging1 on3 ziu3 cyu2 fong1 pui3 hou2 fu3 ngaan5 geng2

rows.note: Use this when the context makes it clear that the medicine being collected or taken is the prescribed medicine.

example.english: I’ll take this prescription medicine when I get home.
example.traditional: 我返到屋企先食呢啲藥。
example.jyutping: ngo5 faan1 dou3 uk1 kei2 sin1 sik6 ni1 di1 joek6

rows.note: Use this mainly in a figurative or elevated context for a remedy or course of treatment.

example.english: This plan is a good prescription for treating this disease.
example.traditional: 呢個方案係醫治呢種病嘅良方。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 fong1 on3 hai6 ji1 zi6 ni1 zung2 beng6 ge3 loeng4 fong1
